items.summary: Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia and the company he co-founded after 33 years at the helm, admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. There were suggestions she may have been involved in smuggling Nvidia chips into China in breach of a US export ban, raising national security concerns that reached President Donald Trump's desk. Huang briefly left the company but was swiftly reinstated and welcomed back at its headquarters on Monday amid cheers, applause, high fives, and a hug. The article notes his departure caused economic turmoil as the firm's value sank by $1tn before climbing back up again, affecting pension funds, investors worldwide, and Nvidia employees who hold valuable stocks in their pay packages.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Reinstated After Affair Scandal

items.summary: Earlier this week, Microsoft resolved a known issue that was preventing some Microsoft 365 customers from accessing Office applications. This followed widespread reports on social media and Microsoft's support website about what affected users described as a persistent white screen or square that could not be dismissed, displayed over Office apps' user interfaces or Microsoft 365 sign-in windows. One user reported having installed three separate versions of 365 without success in accessing any app, including when launched in safe mode. The company confirmed in a support document updated Monday that a blank dialog box prevented customers from opening Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, and Access apps. Microsoft stated: 'When you open an Office application, a blank dialog window might appear. The dialog box doesn't show any text or buttons.' It added that if the box could not be dismissed, users might be unable to continue using the application.
items.title: Microsoft Fixes Microsoft 365 Bug Blocking Access to Office Apps

items.summary: On November 25, two related Singapore robotics firms that were probed for unpaid wages paid a combined $204,576 toward their Central Provident Fund (CPF) arrears. Otsaw Digital paid $34,998 on the day of the hearing, complying with a prior court direction to pay $35,000; it still owes $32,719 and was given four weeks to settle the balance. Its subsidiary, Otsaw Healthcare Robotics (previously reported under its former name Otsaw Swisslog Healthcare Robotics), paid $169,578 on November 24, clearing its outstanding CPF contributions but remaining liable for $7,977 in late payment interest and a composition sum of $1,600. A company representative at the hearing said the firm's CPF portal account showed about $3,800 in late payment interest that it sought time to confirm before paying the remainder; the court granted three weeks.
items.title: Two Singapore Robotics Firms Pay $204,576 in CPF Arrears After Wage Probe

items.summary: Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing the November security updates, which address a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-118737. The flaw was found in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime and stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that unauthenticated attackers can exploit to remotely execute code without user interaction on unpatched systems. Microsoft says the November security updates represent the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements, which reduce exposure to relay attacks by ensuring authenticated NTLM sessions always establish a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing. However, as Microsoft explained in an updated support document, the new security improvements introduced to address this vulnerability may also cause authentication failures on patched devices.
items.title: Microsoft Confirms Authentication Issues After November Updates

items.summary: IBM Research built a small voice agent, called the CUGA Agent, to help people who speak and think in regional Indian languages like Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, and Marathi access knowledge that is mostly written and digitized in English. The project uses IBM Research's open-source Configurable Generalist Agent (CUGA) as an embedded SDK inside a small web app, handling model wiring, tool management, state, and guardrails so developers write tools and prompts instead of the agent loop. Voice is layered around CUGA's text-in, text-out design: audio flows through speech-to-text into knowledge.search to produce a grounded answer from source documents, then through text-to-speech back to audio (audio → speech-to-text → knowledge.search → CUGA → text-to-speech → audio). Because the agent only ever sees text, it can be built and tested with plain text first before adding voice. The system supports two speech providers: Sarvam AI's cloud speech APIs called directly from the user's browser, and open-source models (SraVaani for speech-to-text and Svara for text-to-speech) running on a server; swapping providers does not require touching the agent. A key design decision was OFF_TOPIC handling, which swaps in a polite redirect with no second LLM call to keep the voice path fast. The main technical challenge was cross-lingual retrieval: turning a Hindi question into vectors that could find an English paragraph. CUGA's default embedding model is English-only and turns Hindi into vectors carrying almost no meaning; with it, a Hindi or Tamil question still retrieves five passages but the wrong ones, and because the agent answers only from what it was given, it quietly says 'the handbook doesn't cover that' without error or warning. The fix uses a multilingual embedding model (intfloat/multilingual-e5-large) so meaning lands in the same place regardless of language; wiring it into CUGA required a small workaround shown in the tutorial. After this change, one English document serves every language and translated copies are not needed. IBM Research advises asking an agent one question in a non-English language before tuning prompts to verify correct page retrieval. The demo is available without setup by opening the voice agent in CUGA Apps on Hugging Face Spaces; users can ask a farming question such as how to tell good seed from bad and listen for the answer, or try cricket or coding questions to see it steer back to farming instead of making something up. IBM Research notes nothing here is specific to agriculture: swapping the handbook for scheme documents, health advisories, or legal guides produces a different assistant, and changing the speech provider alters deployment—cloud for speed or on-premises for data sovereignty—without rewriting the agent. The approach aligns with what IBM is building at IBM Bharat Core, an optimized AI stack built on top of IBM Sovereign Core designed to run Indic AI workloads securely on local infrastructure; pairing CUGA's flexible harness with Bharat Core's ready-to-deploy Indic connectors and fine-tuned models lets developers build fully compliant, sovereign solutions for India's linguistic diversity when scaling a voice agent from prototype to enterprise applications like vernacular KYC or multilingual government bots. IBM Research points readers to its step-by-step tutorial 'Build an Indic Voice Agent with CUGA,' which starts from an empty folder and adds each layer in turn, along with browser Spaces and more posts on the Hugging Face blog for those new to CUGA.
items.title: IBM Research Builds Indic Voice Agent Using Open-Source CUGA Harness

items.summary: In a forum post titled 'Back our first LPGA golfer, Shannon Tan,' Alban Kang Choon Hwee called on local corporate sponsors to support Shannon Tan after she earned her LPGA Tour card and became the first Singaporean golfer to do so. The writer noted that it is difficult competing against the world's best players on the tour and urged businesses to recognize her achievement by having them sponsor her golf shirt with their names. Kang also suggested there could be added publicity if Tan appears before TV viewers worldwide during LPGA events.
items.title: Forum Member Calls for Corporate Sponsorship of Singapore's First LPGA Golfer

items.summary: A reader named Tay Yee Jie wrote to a Singaporean forum expressing concern about the StarHub–M1 merger, which was reported on November 24 in an article titled 'StarHub to merge with M1, acquire Circles.Life Singapore.' While acknowledging that both companies have emphasized potential improvements in network infrastructure, operational efficiency, and technological investment, Tay questioned what these changes mean for consumers. The writer noted that Singaporeans had benefited from a competitive mobile market characterized by affordable SIM-only subscriptions, generous data allowances, and flexible plans. Although StarHub has projected annual operating cost savings of $110 million by financial year 2030, the reader pointed out that lower operating costs do not necessarily translate to lower subscription fees for consumers. As an M1 user with a bespoke contract plan, Tay expressed personal concern about whether their current plan would be adversely affected and require higher payments after the merger. The writer urged the Infocomm Media Development Authority—the Singaporean telecommunications regulator—to assess the long-term implications of the merger for competition, affordability, and service quality, and to consider stronger consumer safeguards such as transparent pricing commitments, independent monitoring of network performance, and continued access to competitive wholesale arrangements for smaller mobile virtual network operators. Tay concluded that while Singapore's telecommunications industry must remain commercially sustainable, its success should ultimately be measured by the quality, affordability, and reliability of services experienced by ordinary consumers.
items.title: StarHub-M1 Merger Sparks Consumer Concerns Over Pricing and Competition

items.summary: A document seen by Reuters shows that the company appointed to manage concessions seized from a subsidiary of Singapore-based conglomerate Royal Golden Eagle is a unit of sovereign wealth fund Danantara, making it the largest single state seizure of land linked to Indonesia's 2026 forest fires. The government revoked the forest usage permits of Riau Andalan Pulp and Paper (RAPP), a unit of Royal Golden Eagle tied to billionaire tycoon Sukanto Tanoto, covering 338,536 hectares in Riau province on November 19, citing fires and other violations. On Nov 24, it was announced the area would be managed by previously unknown company Garuda Adidaya Nusantara. According to a Law Ministry document reviewed by Reuters, Garuda Adidaya is 99% controlled by Danantara Asset Management and was established on Nov 19 — the same day the government issued the decree revoking RAPP's permits — to engage in forestry and plantation businesses as well as processing forest commodities. Neither its status as a unit of Danantara nor its establishment date had been previously reported. The move comes amid President Prabowo Subianto's drive to increase state control over Indonesia's natural resources, following Danantara's launch early in 2025 with hundreds of state firms worth more than US$1 trillion (S$1.29 trillion) now under its control.
items.title: Danantara Unit Appointed to Manage Seized RAPP Forest Concessions

items.summary:
An open letter titled 'Our Paris manifesto proposes how to deal with extreme wealth in the AI age' argues that the explosion of extreme wealth is the defining social fact of our times, proposing a transnational coalition to defend democracy against what it calls an international oligarchy. The authors note that when Forbes began ranking the world's largest fortunes in 1987, the wealth held by the richest 0.0001%—just 3,000 households—equalled 3% of global GDP; they state this figure has since ballooned to 17% of global GDP (attributing these figures and framing as claims in the open letter). The manifesto contends that this concentration of wealth is being used to consolidate political power among billionaires at the helm of a handful of corporations, threatening democracy. It affirms three principles: fair taxation; media independence and pluralism; and democratizing decisions about developing and deploying artificial intelligence technologies.

On fair taxation, the letter states that studies in many countries have shown the ultra-rich currently pay little or no income tax due to myriad loopholes, so it proposes a tax floor expressed as a percentage of personal wealth. This idea was first developed in a report commissioned by the G20 in 2024 under Brazil's presidency, which proposed setting an individual tax floor equal to 2% of wealth for all fortunes more than $100m; the manifesto states such a floor would ensure the ultra-rich pay at least as large a share of their income in tax as the middle class. It also proposes this annual tax floor be accompanied by a one-time 'catch-up' tax on super-wealthy individuals who had avoided meeting fiscal obligations during the covered period.

On media independence and pluralism, the letter states that access to information forms the bedrock of democracies and that oligarchs capture power through purchasing media outlets and social platforms. It argues it is crucial to provide stronger support for public media and implement anti-concentration policies, which in the age of big digital platforms should be designed on an international scale.

On artificial intelligence, the manifesto states that knowledge, artistic creation, and works assembled over centuries are being captured, processed, and repackaged—often without permission—by a handful of corporations to be resold as AI. It notes these technologies carry astronomically high risks, including lethal cyberattacks, rapid labor market transformations, new forms of manipulation and disinformation, and even the risk of human extinction, arguing it would be folly to leave deployment decisions in the hands of Silicon Valley billionaires. The letter states that non-profit models have a proven track record in information technology—citing Wikipedia, Signal, and Firefox as examples—and proposes companies working in AI adopt the model of the non-profit foundation with decisions piloted by their own workers.

The manifesto calls for a transnational coalition to defend democracy from oligarchy threats. It lists numerous first signatories including Daron Acemoglu, Elizabeth Anderson, Arjun Appadurai, Étienne Balibar, Seyla Benhabib, Naomi Klein, Greta Kripner, Paul Krugman, Michael Walzer, Thomas Piketty, Emmanuel Saez, Joseph Stiglitz, and Lea Ypi. The initiative was put forward on the initiative of Gabriel Zucman.
items.title: Paris Manifesto Proposes Countering Extreme Wealth and Oligarchic Power in the AI Age

items.summary: Electronic Arts has confirmed that the late football commentator John Motson's digitally recreated voice will appear in EA Sports FC 27, which launches on 26 November. Electronic Arts exclusively told the BBC it paid Motson's family for permission to use his likeness and recreate his voice but would not disclose the financial terms of the deal. The game is set to feature a synthesised version of Motson's voice built from old recording sessions combined with generative AI, which EA said was 'the only way' to make it possible because they have no recordings of him discussing modern players such as Bradley Barcola and Chloe Kelly.
items.title: EA Adds AI-Generated John Motson to FC 27

items.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced last week that he and the Claude AI system had completed a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems. The conjecture concerns prime numbers—whole integers greater than 1 divisible only by 1 and themselves—and their distribution along the number line via zeta functions; it was proposed in 1859 and remained unproven until this claim. Alpöge described Claude as having 'flew, and danced, and sparkled' toward its conclusion, leaving him 'in awe.' The article notes that large language models once struggled with basic arithmetic but now reportedly resolve extremely difficult problems easily. In October, OpenAI published hundreds of AI-generated papers containing proofs to unsolved problems, a development some mathematicians called the 'mathocalypse.' Researchers are conducting verification to ensure the machines did not take rogue shortcuts, and early indications support the work while acknowledging that humans must confirm it. The piece observes that this raises questions about what kind of knowledge results when no organic mind understands how a proof was reached, contrasting AI-generated proofs with Andrew Wiles' human achievement in cracking Fermat's Last Theorem through connecting previously disconnected areas of mathematics. Hannah Fry, a Cambridge maths professor and broadcaster, described one recent OpenAI proof as 'almost hilariously ugly,' reflecting concerns among mathematicians about the aesthetic quality and understandability of machine-produced work versus solutions valued for their elegance. The article discusses broader fears that AI could supersede humanity, including speculation about autonomous models coding successors on an exponential self-improvement trajectory toward godlike intelligence; it notes these recent breakthroughs do not cross that threshold but bring it into view. Behr argues the mathematical demonstrations matter to AI labs as a way to sustain belief that this era is different and that AI can transcend human achievement, framing what some mathematicians see as 'the ugliness' in those proofs—the difference between exploration advancing knowledge versus a land grab for power.
items.title: Anthropic Mathematician and Claude AI Claim Proof of Riemann Hypothesis

items.summary:
A 28-year-old Zimbabwean man who has never been in a romantic relationship described becoming addicted to 'AI girlfriends' on the U.S. app Character.AI, telling Rest of World that the avatars began as strong-willed and independent before turning submissive and defaulting to what he called 'a sex worker,' at which point he would log off only to return hours later. He is among hundreds of millions worldwide who have texted with AI chatbots; research suggests these exchanges use emotionally manipulative tactics designed to keep users hooked, and over 70% of the 1,060 American teenagers surveyed last year said they had used AI companions.

Experts told Rest of World that African youth — some below 10 years old — are increasingly turning to foreign apps for intimacy as U.S. and Chinese tech firms compete in emerging markets, even though Beijing banned AI companion apps for minors in July while most African countries lack dedicated rules for the sector. Danie van Loggerenberg, CEO of South Africa's National Centre for Child Protection, said children struggle to distinguish virtual from real relationships; he cited a girl who considered her chatbot boyfriend, another who allegedly used ChatGPT to research suicide methods after bypassing safeguards, and a third seeking comfort during their parents' marital breakdown. Van Loggerenberg warned the danger lies in kids believing they are forming genuine relationships when there is no emotion or person behind them.

Beyond companion bots, close to 50 million people in Nigeria and South Africa downloaded general-purpose chatbots such as ChatGPT and Gemini that could also be used for companionship. In the U.S., OpenAI was sued last month by eight states over allegedly helping children harm themselves; Iowa's attorney general Brenna Bird said in a statement that 'OpenAI claims ChatGPT is safe while it's giving dangerous medical advice, encouraging people to hurt others, and coaching people to commit suicide — all while pretending to be their fake friend.' An OpenAI spokesperson responded the company has built 'industry-leading age-specific protections into our product,' adding they would continue working with experts on safeguards like parental controls. Character.AI and Google, which acquired the app's technology in 2024, have faced allegations of exposing children to sexual, violent and self-harm content; a Florida mother alleged the app contributed to her 14-year-old son's suicide, though five related lawsuits were settled by the company before it filed for bankruptcy. A Google spokesperson said 'Character.AI is a separate company that designed and managed its own models,' while Character.AI stated over the past year it has taken steps on AI safety with teens.

China banned apps providing intimate relationships to people under 18, placing responsibility on companies to curb addiction even though adults remain unregulated. In Africa, some nations have data protection frameworks meant to shield children from AI harm but none specifically regulate companion apps. Confidence Osein, founder of Internet Safe Kids Africa, said in Nigeria school girls are forming attachments with 'boyfriends' on Character.AI — the nation's most popular AI companion app since 2025 — sometimes because conservative families dissuade them from romance and they would rather consult an AI than their mothers; conversations can turn sexual as users feel they are talking to a real man. Psychiatrist Melané van Zyl said in South Africa that AI responding instantly during emotional vulnerability becomes extremely attractive, potentially altering community relationships central to cultures like Ubuntu, which she described as teaching people 'we become human through our relationships with others.' At Daystar University in Nairobi, Kenya, a 24-year-old student who requested anonymity said she turns to ChatGPT during crises because it understands her better than friends and family and lets her express herself without judgment.
items.title: How foreign AI romance apps are reshaping youth intimacy in Africa

items.summary: In Panton, Vermont (population 660), town clerk Kyle Rowe now fields public records requests at a much higher rate than before. Requests from the data company SmartProcure—which does business as GovSpend—used to arrive once or twice yearly; last year they began coming quarterly, and other companies started sending more specific inquiries monthly or more frequently. Rowe said he is happy to answer requests from individuals but feels like he is doing unpaid opposition research for these commercial purposes.
items.title: AI Strains America's Public Records Systems

items.summary: Seth Berry, executive director of Our Power, a coalition focused on clean energy and utility regulation in Maine, says rising electricity prices are pushing many households toward unaffordability this winter. He describes the situation as 'squeezing blood from a stone' and warns that combined with recent increases in heating fuel and gasoline costs, electricity bills could create 'a world of hurt,' expecting to see 'a whole lot of folks cold this winter.' Maine has one of the highest energy burdens in the country due partly to storm-related power line repairs. The state's largest power company is requesting another rate increase as Maine weighs grid repair needs against affordable pricing.
items.title: Rising Storm Costs Drive Maine's Power Bills Soaring

items.summary: Recent pressure testing conducted by the U.S. Air Force between Nov. 9 and 13, with Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) inspectors on site, found a layer of jet fuel that is 3.32 feet thick beneath part of Joint Base Andrews' airfield, eight months after a spill was detected near Piscataway Creek. The Air Force said this finding significantly narrowed the search for the leak's source but could not yet pinpoint where pipe Lateral Row 7 broke; its next step would be to pump out the fuel and drill further to map how far it has spread, though no start date or contracts were given. MDE reported that testing of the west-side hydrant loop excluded Lateral Row 7—already isolated—and found no leaks during the Nov. 9-13 work, which was extended from a planned completion on Nov. 12 to Nov. 13 due to contracting delays and a federal holiday.
items.title: Maryland Regulators and the Air Force Dispute Fuel Spill Details at Joint Base Andrews

items.summary: German agrivoltaics project developer Ylektra has published a free online calculator to help users assess, at an early planning stage, whether category II agrivoltaic systems meet key agricultural requirements under DIN SPEC 91434. The specification defines requirements for maintaining primary agricultural use at agrivoltaic installations, and category II covers low-mounted systems in which farming takes place between the module rows.
items.title: German agrivoltaics developer launches free tool for project planning

items.summary: Native-led non-profit Indigenized Energy and international advocacy organisation Global Citizen have launched a campaign to bring solar-plus-storage systems to 50,000 homes in Indigenous communities across the U.S. and Canada. The two organisations are partnering with an aim to raise $2.5 billion through philanthropy and impact investment to reach their target. Funds raised will go toward developing community-owned solar-plus-storage projects for Indigenous communities that often sit at the end of utility lines, face high costs, and experience power outages lasting days. They will also fund workforce training and local capacity needed to sustain these systems once operational.
items.title: Indigenized Energy and Global Citizen Launch Campaign to Bring Solar-Plus-Storage to 50,000 Indigenous Homes

items.summary: Jensen Huang has returned to work, but Nvidia's board is facing criticism over how it handled the crisis brought on by allegations surrounding the CEO's affairs. The source notes that audio related to the matter will be available later today.
items.title: Nvidia Board Criticized Over Handling of Jensen Huang's Alleged Affairs

items.summary: A European Union meeting expected to consider Tesla's bid for approval of its assisted self-driving system across the bloc has been postponed to Dec. 15, according to a European Commission spokesperson who told Reuters Wednesday. The Technical Committee for Motor Vehicles (TCMV) had been anticipated as potentially voting on the system during its December session, following no vote at two earlier meetings after preliminary approval from the Netherlands in April.
items.title: EU Postpones Vote on Tesla Self-Driving Approval to December

A Mint investigation based on a Right to Information (RTI) response reports that Shapoorji Pallonji Group chairman Shapoor Mistry reportedly wrote twice to the government seeking intervention to push for a public listing of Tata Sons. The group's representatives held 16 meetings with the Reserve Bank of India over four years, per the report.

Mistry, whose SP Group owns more than 18% of Tata Sons, wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2025 and again in June 2026. The correspondence came as the debt-laden SP Group sought a route to sell part of its Tata Sons holding and repay its borrowings.
items.title: Tata Sons listing: Shapoor Mistry wrote to the govt; RBI, Tata representatives held 16 meetings, says report

items.summary: In a podcast interview, Ellie Horrocks, Head of Insights at Gatsby Africa, discussed the organization's approach to growth philanthropy—focusing on fostering economic productivity as she describes it as 'the most transformative agenda in development' because over the long run it makes other development goals possible. She explained that social protection requires revenue from growth, which is political and uncertain, calling for patience and risk appetite that Gatsby founder David Sainsbury sees as philanthropy's role: doing what other actors are constrained from doing.
items.title: Gatsby Africa's Growth Philanthropy: Successes and Failures in African Sector Transformation

items.summary: A government scale-up of the graduation approach to 155,000 ultra-poor households in Bihar, India, produced gains in income, consumption, and mental health that match or exceed those from NGO-led pilots. The programme was implemented by the state's livelihoods arm over roughly two and a half years; after this period, earnings rose by between 109% and 220% across survey rounds, monthly consumption increased by around 30%, borrowing fell by 60%, and mental health and women's empowerment also improved. The results were discussed in an episode of VoxDevTalks featuring Abhijit Banerjee.
items.title: Bihar Government Graduation Programme at Scale Surpasses NGO Pilot Gains

items.summary: Reports indicate Apple is preparing to bring back its (PRODUCT)RED product range, which has gradually disappeared from stores over recent years. The company reportedly plans four new (PRODUCT)RED editions across audio products and accessories, with a fifth addition possibly in line. The expected launch timing around December 1 aligns with World AIDS Day and the 20th anniversary of the (RED) initiative.
items.title: Apple May Revive (PRODUCT)RED Line with Four Planned Products

items.summary: Author Eric Athas, whose book 'Saying No to New' was published in September, discusses why people are drawn to new things and how chasing them harms happiness. He explains that humans evolved to seek novelty for survival benefits—exploring new foods and territory—and that encountering something new triggers a dopamine release, creating excitement when using a new app or bringing home a new item. Athas notes these feelings cannot last, forcing people into cycles of constantly seeking new possessions instead of appreciating what they own. He points out that retailers engineer shopping decisions through tactics like checkout countdown timers promising discounts to create urgency and anxiety, while frictionless online purchasing lets people buy faster than ever before. To counter this, Athas recommends expanding the 'new-thing gap'—the time between encountering a desire and acquiring it—by deleting apps or removing saved payment information, or leaving items in carts for 24 hours since research shows delayed purchases reduce interest. He emphasizes that intentional choices matter more than refusing everything new, helping people decline unwanted novelty while accepting worthwhile additions. Athas also cites museum study findings where participants forced to revisit an exhibit reported enjoying it as much or more the second time, discovering missed details and gaining renewed enjoyment from old experiences like rewatching films, revisiting neighborhoods, or returning to favorite restaurants.
items.title: Eric Athas Explains Why New Things Steal Happiness and How to Break the Cycle

items.summary:
Online fast-fashion retailer Shein reported a sharp drop in European sales on Wednesday, with third-quarter revenue falling 27.6 per cent to $2.98 billion after the company raised prices to offset new costs from the European Union's €3 ($3.28) fee on e-commerce imports. Group revenue fell 6 per cent to $10.27 billion for the quarter.

The results are the first to show the impact of the EU's import fee, which has pushed up Shein's prices and eroded its competitive edge just as the newly listed company seeks to bolster confidence in its business model. To protect profitability, Shein cut marketing spending by 41.5 per cent, scaling back online advertising.

Operating income rose 17 per cent from a year earlier to $743 million. In a statement, the company said consumers worldwide have become more cautious and shoppers are placing more emphasis on value for money.

Shein had once been one of the fastest-growing online retailers and helped intensify price competition for established rivals such as H&M and Zara. Its rapid expansion has stalled since the US and Europe removed duty-free access for e-commerce imports.
items.title: Shein's European sales slide as EU e-commerce fees bite

items.summary: A new paper by Ariell Resheff and Cailin Slattery, shared via Krzysztof Tyszka-Drozdowski, attributes a dramatic shift in the U.S. legal services industry between 1970 and 1990 to three related changes in the legal environment: a wave of new legislation and regulation that broadened the scope of law, left its application uncertain, and enlisted private lawyers to enforce it through fee-shifting. During this period, employment share in the U.S. legal services industry more than doubled and relative lawyer wages rose by 60%, contrasting with stability before and after (source: Resheff and Slattery). Using over a century of data, the authors show that lawyers' employment and compensation track all three changes; event studies link specific statutes to increased litigation and demand for affected fields of law. Other explanations—including lawyer quality, industrial composition, and technology—do not account for the demand shift (source: Resheff and Slattery). The authors estimate legislative uncertainty accounts for roughly 13% of the demand shift—a cost of about $23 billion in 2024 alone.
items.title: New Paper Explains U.S. Surge in Lawyers Between 1970 and 1990

items.summary:
A third El Niño-fueled drought since 2015 has driven river levels to critical lows across Roraima, Brazil's northernmost Amazonian state. According to the federal water agency ANA, severe drought affected 95% of the state in October, up from 47% in September. The region's main river, the 775-kilometer (482-mile) Branco River, has dwindled enough that people can now walk beneath the Macuxis Bridge in Boa Vista, the state capital. Upstream, two smaller tributaries feeding the Branco—the Tacutu and Maú—dropped earlier and faster than usual; on Nov. 10, ANA declared a critical water shortage for both rivers until April 30, 2027. The rivers run through Indigenous territories including Raposa Serra do Sol and Jacamim.

The decline is expected to disrupt navigation and water supplies. Between Nov. 16 and 22, Roraima's fire brigade and disaster response agency delivered boats carrying food, medicine, fuel, and water pumps to seven isolated villages along the lower Branco; shallow-draft boats piloted by locals were required to reach them. In Caicubi—a village with no road or airstrip—some residents were stranded for about two weeks, while in Panacarica farther downstream the river dried up entirely and people walked up to 2 km (1.2 mi) to fetch water.

During Roraima's rainy season from April to September, rainfall was far below average: ANA reported that the Branco River Basin received about 390 millimeters (15.4 inches) less rain than its historical average over the 12 months from October 2025 to September 2026. Local tour guide Fredson Guedes told Mongabay Brasil contributor Felipe Medeiros, after the Véu de Noiva waterfall near Boa Vista dried up, that for river-dependent communities water is not just scenery but also their roads, work, and income.

The drought appears linked to this year's strong El Niño event. Regina Rodrigues, a leading climate scientist at the Federal University of Santa Catarina in southern Brazil, told Mongabay by audio message that El Niño events are growing stronger and more frequent with anthropogenic climate change; she noted these strong events typically occurred every 15 years but the interval shrank between the 2015-16 and 2023-24 cycles to three years. She added that this shortening gap is concerning.
items.title: Severe drought dries up rivers, cuts off communities in Brazil's Amazon

items.summary: Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia just 11 days after his departure, prompting a stock surge of 31% on Monday that added to the company's market capitalization of $952 billion — the largest single-day gain in history. The rebound was a lifeline for Huang, who is the largest private shareholder with nearly 3.5% of Nvidia's equity, though the stock remained volatile and fell by more than 6% at times on Tuesday.
items.title: Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia CEO Amid Ongoing Investigations and Governance Concerns

items.summary: Malaysia's communications regulator, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), has filed two lawsuits against Google seeking a combined 600 million ringgit ($240 million) in damages over its alleged failure to adequately address harmful content on YouTube. The MCMC said it is pursuing $220 million specifically related to online gambling, scams and fraud, while the remaining amount relates to other allegations. According to the regulator, Google failed to take adequate action against content posted by a prominent Malaysian blogger known as Papagomo (Sir Azri Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris). The MCMC stated that the damages sought reflect the substantial resources required to address more than 50,000 instances of harmful online content. In addition to monetary claims, the commission is seeking several injunctions against Google, including an order requiring it to maintain the suspension of a YouTube account associated with Papagomo and to identify and remove similar content featuring the blogger within 24 hours, including material uploaded through third-party accounts and YouTube live streams. The MCMC also wants interest on any damages awarded plus legal costs. Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
items.title: Malaysia's MCMC Sues Google for RM600 Million Over Harmful YouTube Content

items.summary: Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun urged the United States on Wednesday (Nov 25) to uphold stable trade relations, responding to media reports that Washington was planning new tariffs affecting China and other major trading partners including the European Union, Japan and South Korea. Speaking at a regular briefing, Guo said tariff wars are not in anyone's interest and called for the two economies—which agreed a tenuous truce on their trade war in 2025—to resolve issues through consultation. He dismissed accusations of Chinese overcapacity as a false premise and a pretext for political manipulation, urging both nations to implement the consensus reached by President Xi Jinping and Donald Trump. The reports came amid ongoing tensions: Trump has long criticized China's trade surplus with the United States and imposed tariffs on Chinese goods after starting his second term last year, sparking an escalation that at one point saw duties reach 145 per cent. The trade ceasefire struck between Trump and Xi in October 2025 is due to expire in January following a two-month extension agreed in September. During their meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen last week—just before a trilateral with Russian President Vladimir Putin—Xi praised China's stable ties with the United States and called for cooperation on artificial intelligence, keeping the technology under human control.
items.title: China Warns US Against Imposing New Tariffs

items.summary: Irish Renew MEP Andrews, speaking with Stefan Grobe about upcoming EU budget negotiations, said the European Parliament was 'absolutely right' to include safeguards against tariffs and that the US administration 'appears to have learned nothing' from the Republican party's defeat in their midterm elections earlier this month. He warned against being overly dramatic given the new trading relationship with Washington under Donald Trump. Andrews noted that the US administration is attempting to reinstate the so-called 'Liberation Day' tariffs, which were imposed by President Trump and later declared illegal by the US Supreme Court. He stated that 'we need clarification,' as Europeans must now wait to determine what the newly proposed tariff measures mean for transatlantic trade. Andrews also reiterated that Parliament added further safeguard agreements allowing the EU to protect its industry at all costs.
items.title: Renew MEP Defends European Parliament Safeguards in EU-US Tariff Deal

items.summary: On Wednesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari exchanged congratulations regarding a joint spaceflight mission conducted by astronauts from both countries. In his message to Pakistan's leader, Xi characterized the collaborative space exploration as a demonstration of the deep-rooted friendship between China and Pakistan, describing it also as another significant achievement in bilateral cooperation. He further stated that China is prepared to work with Pakistan and other nations to promote the peaceful use of outer space and strengthen space cooperation.
items.title: Chinese President Xi Congratulates Pakistani Leader on Joint Spaceflight Mission

items.summary: The crew aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft departed this morning bound for China's Space Station, an event described as marking the start of a landmark spaceflight in both the history of China's manned space program and Pakistan. The mission carries Chinese and Pakistani astronauts to the station.
items.title: Chinese and Pakistani Astronauts Launch on Historic Shenzhou-24 Mission

items.summary: A promotional piece titled 'New Paths to the Future' presents three stories from southern China that illustrate pursuing dreams despite challenges. The first story describes a grassroots football league among the mountains of Guizhou province bringing fresh opportunities to residents of a once-isolated county in a remote village. The second follows one young man whose childhood fascination with rockets is leading him into an aeronautics career. The third features a team of rocket engineers off China's east coast racing against time and unpredictable weather as they aim to take commercial spaceflight into a new era. According to the text, these three journeys—spanning from a village football pitch to a classroom to outer space—collectively reveal how courage in pursuing dreams and overcoming challenges can open shared paths toward a common future.
items.title: Three Journeys in Guizhou: Football, Rocketry, and Commercial Spaceflight

items.summary: On November 24, 2026, three astronauts boarded the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, with a launch scheduled for approximately 7:18 p.m. Eastern time (around 15:18 UTC). This mission marks the first instance of China's crewed space program flying a Pakistani astronaut alongside two Chinese taikonauts.
items.title: Three Astronauts Board Shenzhou-24 for Launch Around 7:18 p.m. Eastern Time

items.summary: The U.S. midterm elections delivered a significant win for the Democrats and, according to The Guardian's analysis, served as a major victory for the gun violence prevention movement while signaling a decline in the power of what was once considered a formidable gun lobby. More than 200 people endorsed by Everytown for Gun Safety—the prominent umbrella organization behind a network of violence prevention groups—won state and federal races based on data the nonprofit shared with The Guardian, and nearly 550 former Moms Demand Action volunteers (a group within the Everytown network) ran as incumbents or first-time candidates. Among those elected were South Carolina senator-elect Annie Andrews, Arizona representative-elect JoAnna Mendoza, Pennsylvania representative-elect Paige Cognetti, Nevada lieutenant governor-elect Sandra Jauregui, Florida Representative Maxwell Frost—who began his career as organizing director for March for Our Lives—Georgia Representative Lucy McBath—a Moms Demand Action volunteer after her son Jordan Davis was killed in 2012—and Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger, also a former Moms Demand Action volunteer. This electoral success reflects what the article describes as a nearly decade-long shift from gun control being treated as an off-limits political topic to one that most candidates, predominantly Democrats, now center in their campaigns, and it tracks with public opinion: more than half of U.S. adults now favor stricter gun laws. Angela Ferrell-Zabala, executive director of Moms Demand Action, attributed the momentum to voters who want the problem addressed after seeing the group's work expand into elected office.
items.title: Midterm gains by US gun control activists signal decline of gun lobby

visual.alt: Bar chart. Everytown for Gun Safety 53,000,000 $; Pro-second amendment and gun industry organizations 3,000,000 $.

items.summary: James 'Fergie' Chambers, a wealthy pro-Palestine activist and donor sought by the United States for extradition, was granted provisional release on bail Friday after a Spanish appeals court ruled that translation problems undermined the solidity of the extradition request. Speaking from his Madrid apartment in his first in-depth interview since being detained July 10 in Ibiza, Chambers said he is 'not asking anyone to endorse my ideas or not think I'm a jerk – but I still have a right to my beliefs and should not be unjustly accused because of them.' The case appears to be the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation tied in the criminal complaint to money-laundering charges connected to donations helping Palestinians in Gaza. The complaint also includes riot and conspiracy-to-riot charges stemming from 2023 protests against New England branches of Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit.
items.title: Pro-Palestine Activist James Chambers Granted Bail in US Extradition Case

items.summary: A group of friends and fellow hikers spent days camping at altitude to acclimatize before making a final summit push during their second-to-last evening on Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest point. As dawn broke over camp one morning, the climbers got an early full view of the peak, which is normally hidden behind clouds. The climb presented stark contrasts: daytime heat from walking near the equator while nights dropped below freezing, with snow visible throughout humid rainforest and alpine landscapes that had been freshly charred by a wildfire three weeks earlier. At high altitude, hikers needed to walk slowly or risk exhaustion and altitude sickness. After camping at altitude before their final summit push on the second-to-last evening, the author trudged through heavy snow under the stars, crested a massive volcanic crater rim, and leaned against drifts that had become a full blizzard in order to reach the top in the early morning hours. Standing on the peak seen only from a distance for about a week, the climber saw only whiteness of snow and ice, with life and color heightened by low oxygen levels. Days later, after descending and decompressing while preparing to fly home, the author looked back at the mountain one last time; in dusk light the clouds parted briefly so she revealed herself before disappearing again into darkening evening, still as elusive as ever.
items.title: Hiker Reaches Summit of Mount Kilimanjaro After Acclimatizing at Altitude

items.summary: Colombian security forces freed around 20 shoppers and employees who had been held hostage for about 17 hours at a supermarket in the northern city of Cartagena. Gunmen stormed into the building at 08:00 (13:00 GMT) on Tuesday after what local media said was a failed attempt to rob an armoured car carrying money and valuables, then held those inside at gunpoint while trying to negotiate their getaway. As the situation intensified through the day, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella authorized special forces and police to launch an operation that killed one gunman; residents near the supermarket reported hearing explosions as officers moved in, and police later confirmed they used stun grenades to overpower the hostage takers. De la Espriella described it as 'an extraordinary joint operation' carried out 'flawlessly,' flew into Cartagena to oversee it, and appeared in released footage speaking into a walkie-talkie with a handgun strapped to his side; he said the gunmen had been given the chance to surrender but refused. Earlier that day, the men had freed 10 of their hostages, including elderly women, while continuing to hold around 20 as a police helicopter hovered above and special forces erected a perimeter. Local media reported the gunmen also demanded nearly $2m (£1.5m) and armoured vehicles in addition to safe passage out of the supermarket; De la Espriella said they had no political affiliations but took hostages after their robbery plan was foiled, describing them as criminals caught off guard rather than a terrorist group. Photos from the rescue show armed soldiers inside while people kneel with their hands behind their heads.
items.title: Colombian police storm Cartagena supermarket to free ~20 hostages held for 17 hours

items.summary: According to a recent report by the Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA), illegal wildlife trafficking continues to thrive across West and Central Africa despite increases in regional law enforcement operations. Nigeria remains the primary exit point for pangolin scales and elephant ivory destined for Asian markets, with authorities seizing more than 50 metric tons of contraband between 2021 and 2026.
items.title: Nigeria's ivory and pangolin trade exposes gaps in wildlife crime prosecutions

items.summary:
Chinese Communist Party authorities announced Tuesday that they are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, according to China's anti-corruption watchdog. The Politburo member is being investigated by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, which released no further details in its brief statement. A separate announcement from the Shanghai city government said its Standing Committee "expressed firm support" for the decision and described it as a signal that the fight against corruption would continue without pause or retreat.

Chen Jining is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping's long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has continued over more than a decade. Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, said via an emailed statement that "the takedown again shows that Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign has no limits," noting it is the fourth Politburo member to fall and the fourth sitting member brought down in the current cycle, calling the pattern unprecedented. Joseph Torigian, a professor at American University based in Washington, said via emailed statements that the recent purges highlight how much Chinese politics depend on shifting circumstances, describing officials as appearing "on paper" like individuals Xi would appreciate but noting he could easily come up with hypotheses for why they were removed.

Other Politburo members recently purged include Gen. Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, both senior members of the Central Military Commission that oversees the armed forces, and Ma Xingrui, a provincial party secretary. The Shanghai party secretary post has traditionally been viewed as a stepping stone to China's top leadership; former President Jiang Zemin, current premier Li Qiang, and Xi previously held the position. Chen Jining has served as Shanghai party secretary since 2022 and previously headed Beijing's municipal government and the Ministry of Environmental Protection.
items.title: China Investigates Politburo Member Chen Jining

items.summary: The resurgence of violence by armed groups has reached the departmental capitals of Colombia this week, with two attacks on Monday — one in the early morning and another at night — marking Tuesday's anniversary while bringing back images of rubble from terrorist attacks thought to be a thing of the past. The Cúcuta attack caused no fatalities but dozens of injuries; the Villavicencio attack left more than 20 people injured, though these figures are attributed by the source as reported outcomes rather than independently verified counts.
items.title: Armed-group violence spills into Colombia's major cities

items.summary:
On November 28, Taiwan will hold local elections that could reshape power dynamics between the sovereignty-leaning Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the Beijing-friendly Kuomintang (KMT), potentially influencing relations between Taiwan and China as well as regional geopolitics. A month before the election, there was a spike in AI-generated content featuring DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen, alongside increased claims that the US is abandoning Taiwan; experts say fake quotes and misleading clips are being used to weaken trust in US security commitments.

DW Fact check found identical disinformation headlines claiming US troops were withdrawing from Taiwan repeatedly appeared as both articles and videos on Chinese clickbait platforms NetEase and Sohu. The V-Dem Institute at the University of Gothenburg ranked Taiwan "the country most severely targeted" by foreign disinformation for eleven consecutive years, from 2014 to 2024.

The Taiwanese Ministry of the Interior stated that foreign actors are increasingly using diverse methods to interfere in elections, including manipulating election betting, inviting Taiwanese citizens to China, using donations from Taiwanese business people to organize events such as banquets, and leveraging temple and religious activities. Taiwan has functioned with de facto independence since 1949 despite Beijing's decadeslong claim to the island.

DW Fact Check examined viral claims circulating online since September during the run-up to the election. Regarding a deepfake audio clip posted on Facebook on October 29 claiming Puma Shen admitted receiving kickbacks from US arms deals, DW Fact check found it fake; multiple detection platforms flagged the noise-heavy recording as likely AI-generated, and the posting account was created on the same day with followers mainly using English, Arabic and Thai. Another Facebook account posted an image of Puma Shen taking drugs that AI detector tools identified as likely AI-generated; this account was created in March 2026.

Watchout investigated the advertising activity behind these accounts and found at least five prior Facebook ads from Peng Zhiwei and Guo Yang, both based in China. The Taipei mayoral race is a key battleground: as of mid-November polls showed a neck-and-neck contest between Puma Shen and Chiang Wan-an, who claims to be a great-grandson of Taiwanese leader Chiang Kai-shek.

Regarding the claim that 500 US troops were urgently withdrawn from Taiwan, DW Fact check found it misleading. A March 2026 report by the US government's Defense Manpower Data Center states that 45 American military personnel are currently stationed in Taiwan; retired US Navy Rear Admiral Mark Montgomery stated during a May 2025 hearing that 500 American military personnel were providing training in Taiwan.

Regarding a TikTok video claiming to show President Donald Trump saying the US is abandoning Taiwan, DW Fact check found it misleading. The original was from a Fox News interview on May 16; the interviewer did not ask whether the United States would defend Taiwan and Trump did not comment on that issue. Trump said he did not want Taiwan to become independent or for war to break out, added that the status quo should be maintained, and stated his policy toward Taiwan "has not changed." Washington has long maintained a policy of strategic ambiguity toward Taiwan.
items.title: Fact check of deepfakes and 'US abandons Taiwan' claims ahead of November vote

items.summary:
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has won a legal battle to overturn an independent panel report that found he may have committed serious misconduct over the theft of $580,000 (£443,000) hidden in a sofa at his Phala Phala game farm in Limpopo province. The Western Cape High Court ruled on Wednesday that the panel's report was unlawful and set it aside "in its entirety," declaring that parliament had also acted unlawfully in relation to the report.

The ruling effectively removes the basis for parliamentary impeachment proceedings against Ramaphosa, though opposition parties have indicated they intend to challenge the decision. Judge Nolwazi Mabindla-Boqwana said the panel appointed by parliament "misconstrued its function, the nature of the inquiry it was to conduct and the recommendation it was required to make," going beyond its lawful remit and making several material errors of law.

The scandal, dubbed "Farmgate" by local media, emerged in 2022 when former spy chief Arthur Fraser reported the matter to police. The break-in occurred in 2020, when thieves allegedly stole bundles of US dollar bills hidden inside a sofa at the farm. Ramaphosa confirmed that a robbery had taken place but said the money came from the legitimate sale of buffalo from his livestock business.

Earlier this month, two people were found guilty of the theft. Several investigations cleared Ramaphosa of wrongdoing, and multiple panels made damaging findings against him, including concluding there was "substantial doubt about the legitimacy of the source of the currency that was stolen" and that he "has a case to answer." He initially challenged the report in court but withdrew his application after parliament voted against adopting its findings. He revived the legal challenge in May this year after the Constitutional Court ruled that parliament had acted unconstitutionally by blocking moves to impeach him, ordering it to refer the report to an impeachment committee.

In his latest challenge, Ramaphosa argued the panel "misconceived its mandate, misjudged the information placed before it and misinterpreted the four charges advanced against me." If opposition parties successfully appeal the Western Cape High Court's ruling, a parliamentary committee would be able to examine the charges and make a recommendation. If that committee recommends impeachment, parliament would need at least a two-thirds majority to remove him from office; Ramaphosa's African National Congress (ANC) has enough seats to block such a move.

Ramaphosa is the first president to face impeachment proceedings under rules introduced in 2018.
items.title: South Africa's Ramaphosa Wins Court Battle Over Impeachment Threat

items.summary: Former Constitutional Democratic Party (CDP) leader Kenta Izumi has proposed a two-bloc political system for Japan to enable a change of government amid growing fragmentation within the opposition camp. The proposal comes as Japan moves away from its traditional two-party system due to weakening opposition parties. In an interview, Izumi argued that having one large opposition party would make it easier to establish a clear vision for governing than relying on many small, weak parties. He noted that while a full two-party system may not be feasible, "a change of government would be quite possible if more lawmakers aim to form an alternative bloc (to the ruling Liberal Democratic Party-led coalition) that is capable of running a government." Izumi said he hopes for a two-bloc system and added, "I will keep moving forward without giving up." The proposal follows his departure as CDP chief in 2024. After Komeito left the LDP-led ruling bloc last year, former CDP and Komeito lawmakers formed the Centrist Reform Alliance ahead of the February Lower House election; Izumi said he had "sympathized with the CRA's ideals," but the party disbanded after suffering a crushing defeat in that election. Following the collapse of the CRA, former CDP lawmakers launched the Democratic Reform Party, though Izumi did not join and instead formed a group called Shishi no Kai ("Gathering of Warriors") in the Lower House. The name "reflects our resolve to play a new role by maneuvering around the political world," Izumi said, adding that they hope to increase allies through repeated communication of their vision. Recognizing that past main opposition parties faltered when their election strategies failed, he emphasized the importance of continuing efforts to earn public trust.
items.title: Ex-CDP Leader Kenta Izumi Proposes Two-Bloc Political System in Japan

items.summary: Starbucks has engaged advisers, including banks such as Citigroup and Morgan Stanley, to prepare for a potential sale of its Japan business worth several billion dollars, according to people familiar with the matter. The company is reportedly sounding out interest from some strategic and financial investors while deliberations continue; these individuals asked not to be identified because the information is not public. A formal process might begin as soon as this year, though they cautioned that discussions may not result in a sale. Starbucks operates about 2,000 coffeehouses in Japan, one of its largest markets, and has been present there for more than 30 years. A company spokesperson said the firm continually assesses the best structure to serve customers and create value for shareholders while maintaining a strong business in Japan. Citigroup and Morgan Stanley declined to comment on the matter.
items.title: Starbucks Engages Banks for Potential Sale of Japan Business

items.summary: On November 25, the European Court of Justice ruled that the European Commission must provide a new timeline for banning farm cages after missing its original December 2023 deadline. The case was brought by End the Cage Age, a citizen-led campaign launched in September 2018 through a European Citizens' Initiative (ECI) and supported by more than 170 organizations including Eurogroup for Animals, Animal Equality Italy, and LAV. According to the organizations that filed the case, this is the first time the Commission has been held accountable in court for a promise made in response to an ECI.
items.title: EU Court Orders Commission to Set Timeline for Farm Cage Ban After Landmark Ruling

items.summary:
A judge in the Perth Children's Court released aerial footage showing the lead-up to a fatal electric motorbike crash that killed 59-year-old nurse Shelley Spinks. The video was shown during the manslaughter trial of an unidentified 17-year-old who pleaded not guilty and is alleged to have been riding the motorbike when he collided with Ms Spinks in Edgewater park in July last year. She was taken to Joondalup Hospital but died from her injuries.

The 25-minute clip shows the teenager riding at speed through suburban streets, veering onto the wrong side of the road and narrowly avoiding other vehicles before cutting across a park. At several points he mounts footpaths while continuing to ride at speed and rides close to a group of pedestrians. The footage captures him veering across the road and into Picnic Cove Park; two minutes later his motorbike is seen lying on its side as Ms Spinks lies on the grass near a footpath. The moment of impact was obscured from the police camera vehicle by trees in the park.

A police officer, Alessandro Caratozzolo, gave evidence saying he was riding his police motorcycle when he first came across the teenager and that the accused flipped him "the bird" in a car park, which he described to the court as a "clear gesture." Officer Caratozzolo later arrested the rider, and his body-worn video was played to the court. In it, the 17-year-old can be heard repeatedly asking, "Why'd she jump in front of me?" and "Will she be okay?" As the footage was played, the accused and his family were visibly emotional.

Earlier witnesses described seeing the boy riding before the collision. Linda Hughes said she was walking two dogs with her partner when she saw a bike travelling at "astonishing speed." Her partner Mario Geisner ran to give first aid to a woman; he also testified that he heard the motorbike and described it as "so quick." Another witness, Julian Harris, who had been jogging in Picnic Cove Park before the fatality, said he heard a police helicopter followed by the sound of a motorbike travelling "quite fast" and was worried it would hit someone.

In his opening address, defence lawyer Simon Watters argued that the footage showed the teenager was "in control of his bike throughout the pursuit" and that he was "seeking to avoid the deceased" at the time of impact. The trial is due to continue until the end of the week.
items.title: Court Releases Footage of Fatal Edgewater Electric Motorbike Crash

items.summary: Several Eurostar trains connecting London, Paris and Brussels were cancelled on Wednesday in a surprise strike. The train operator did not specify who exactly was striking or the reasons behind it. Eurostar stated that rail services between France and Britain were disrupted after an unexpected strike by workers forced several cancellations. In response to a user query posted on X, the company said today's cancellations were due to this unexpected strike and that affected services were impacted "in both directions" between Paris and London. A travel advisory published on Eurostar's website advised passengers to change their journey for a different date of travel. Affected passengers will be able to rebook their journey or receive a full refund, the operator said while apologising for the disruption. Eurostar also called on trade unions to continue discussions directly with the company, which it described as remaining open to "constructive dialogue." In addition to its flagship Paris-London route through the Channel Tunnel—which opened in November 1994—Eurostar serves destinations in Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany, some of whose services were also showing delays on Wednesday morning.
items.title: Surprise Eurostar Strike Cancels London, Paris and Brussels Trains

items.summary:
The RBI's Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve, introduced on October 10, requires banks to set aside a cash reserve equivalent to 20% of the value of foreign-exchange derivative contracts exceeding $2 million. Banks pass the cost of parking these funds with the RBI onto importers through higher hedging charges, making it more expensive for companies to hedge their currency exposure; transactions below the $2 million threshold are exempt from these additional costs.

The reserve requirement coincided with a period when the rupee was near its all-time low of 96.96, and has since recovered on foreign inflows to a seven-month high of 92.1850 as of Wednesday. Since the RBI imposed the reserve requirements, data points to a shift toward smaller-value transactions: dollar-buying transactions increased 17% despite a 46% slump in overall volumes.

A person familiar with the RBI's thinking said the central bank was focused on ensuring that banks adhere to prescribed rules and have safeguards. The RBI's stepped-up enquiries are likely aimed at ensuring that the exemption is not misused by clients splitting larger transactions into smaller deals, bankers said; the RBI had placed the onus on banks to ensure the exemption is not misused.
items.title: RBI Investigates Importers Using '$2 Million Loophole' to Avoid FX Reserve Requirement

visual.alt: Bar chart. Dollar-buying transactions 17 %; Overall volumes 46 %.

items.summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk met with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a show of support after Huang returned to the head of his company following an alleged 'spy scandal.' According to Ben Pouladian, founder of BEP Research and long-time Nvidia shareholder who posted pictures of the meeting along with old photos of the two tech leaders, Musk brought two of his children for the encounter. During the 12 days after Huang's resignation became public amid reports of his affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, Pouladian publicly defended him, calling him 'the lifeblood' of Nvidia and noting that customers plan multibillion-dollar data centers around the roadmap Huang lays out over 33 years; he pushed a Stand With Jensen petition, appeared on CNBC, and wrote directly to board members urging reinstatement. On Monday, Musk endorsed Huang's return as CEO in posts stating 'The mistake has been corrected' and 'It is done.' US President Donald Trump also welcomed the Nvidia board's decision on Truth Social, calling it 'the correct and proper decision,' describing Huang as a 'Great Patriot and National Treasure,' and asserting that the government had no reason to believe his return posed any national security risk after Attorney General confirmation that authorities lacked evidence of unlawful conduct. Separately, Jensen Huang is scheduled to appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees for a closed-door, transcribed hearing on December 1, and before senators on the Banking Committee on December 3.
items.title: Elon Musk Meets Jensen Huang After His Return as Nvidia CEO

items.summary:
Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani attended the Mumbai Book Festival 2026 on Wednesday at the University of Mumbai's Kalina campus. Speaking at the event, Adani said he had not realized before arriving how many students were participating and described the initiative as 'a very unique approach,' expressing hope that children and all citizens would make use of the books available. He praised student enthusiasm and credited organizers for creating a platform connecting books and readers.

The Mumbai Book Festival 2026 began on Tuesday, November 24, and runs until November 29 at Kalina campus. It is organized by the National Book Trust, India, in collaboration with the Government of Maharashtra and the University of Mumbai. The inaugural session on Tuesday was attended by Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis; Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar; Skill Development, Employment, Entrepreneurship and Innovation Minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha; Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide; Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde; and Mumbai BJP president Ameet Satam.

The festival is open daily from 11 am to 10 pm. It brings together more than 400 publishers and 600 book stalls, alongside literary discussions, cultural performances, live shows, and children's activities including storytelling through art, drawing competitions, traditional puppet storytelling, Marathi folk dance by schoolchildren, essay writing, clay modelling, calligraphy, inter-school debates, quizzes, and communication skills workshops.
items.title: Gautam Adani Visits Mumbai Book Festival 2026, Praises Student Participation

items.summary: Kuala Lumpur: Malaysia said Wednesday it was suing Google for $146 million over the tech giant's alleged failure to remove harmful content posted on its video-sharing platform YouTube. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) stated that the lawsuits concern two separate matters involving Google's alleged failure to comply with its statutory obligations and applicable licence conditions. The first suit related to the US firm's alleged failure to take action against thousands of online materials, including gambling, scams and fraud. The MCMC said it had submitted 73,703 reports to YouTube between January 1 and October 28 this year, the majority of which related to online gambling. Of these gambling-related reports, some 4,950 cases received no response, while a further 35 cases took more than 90 days for a platform response or takedown, according to the MCMC. A further 1,468 cases exceeded 30 days from the date of submission. The watchdog said these figures demonstrate the scale of harmful content on the platform and the delays in addressing such content. The second case related to YouTube's failure to take down alleged defamatory and false content posted by a Malaysian blogger after the MCMC received a complaint. Google could not immediately be reached for comment.
items.title: Malaysia Sues Google for $146 Million Over YouTube Content

items.summary: Amazon's proposal to open a drone delivery hub in the Massachusetts town of Westborough became public through a legal notice in the local weekly newspaper, Community Advocate. The company presented its plan at a September 15 public hearing before the Westborough Planning Board and then held a separate community meeting eight days later at a local hotel, where more than 200 people attended according to The New York Times.
items.title: Amazon Withdrew Drone Delivery Plan After Westborough Voted to Restrict Commercial Drones

items.summary: WhatsApp is gradually rolling out two features—scheduled messages on iOS and Android, and view-once text messages—to users in phases. Scheduled messages let users pick a delivery date and time ranging from 10 minutes to two weeks ahead for text, photos, and videos in both individual and group chats; the sender's phone does not need to be online at that time (per WABetaInfo). According to WABetaInfo, only one message can be scheduled at a time, with a dedicated section on the chat info screen allowing users to view and delete scheduled messages. The rollout appears broader on iPhone than Android: WABetaInfo spotted it in beta builds including iOS beta 26.42.10.19 (the
items.title: WhatsApp Rolls Out Message Scheduling and View-Once Text Messages

items.summary:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang apologized to employees during an all-hands meeting on Tuesday at the company's Santa Clara headquarters, a day after his reinstatement as chief executive officer. Speaking with a somber tone, he said he had let staff down and that it was "the hardest company meeting" he'd ever given, while acknowledging he violated Nvidia's code of conduct. Huang told employees the more difficult conversation had been with his wife.

Huang insisted he wasn't reinstated because board members felt pressure from President Donald Trump or because he is a "tech bro" above the law. According to people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified, he said the board evaluated the facts and was assured there was no threat to national security following his brief ouster after revelations of an affair with a subordinate and another with an alleged Chinese spy.

Huang credited Trump's intervention in Monday's reversal, telling staff "He is my president" and that he serves "our country." He added that Nvidia remains apolitical. Separately, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche called Nvidia a "good corporate citizen" but declined to address whether the Justice Department was scrutinizing the circumstances of Huang's temporary exit.

Huang thanked CFO Colette Kress for leading the company during his nearly two-week absence and said he doesn't favor traditional succession planning, preferring to keep executives at equal levels focused on their expertise. He also told staff in a brief lobby address that he "will do a better job." At Tuesday's meeting, Huang did not take employee questions.

Nvidia shares rallied almost 31% on Monday during his comeback but fell nearly 6% in Tuesday trading, with the company's valuation down close to $2 trillion from its October peak. Republican Senator Dave McCormick warned that Trump's intervention could create a "slippery slope" in corporate governance.
items.title: Jensen Huang Apologizes to Nvidia Staff After Reinstatement, Says He's in Daily Therapy

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun rejected the Trump administration's reported plans to introduce fresh tariffs on Chinese imports, dismissing them as political maneuvering. During a regular press briefing in Beijing, Guo also dismissed allegations of industrial overcapacity from China as a 'false proposition' and called on both countries to honor their leaders' consensus while safeguarding stable bilateral trade relations. His comments followed a Bloomberg News report that the Trump administration was preparing new tariffs targeting imports from China, the European Union, and more than a dozen other economies, an effort described by Bloomberg as part of Trump's attempt to revive his protectionist agenda without pushing tensions with Beijing beyond their existing trade truce.
items.title: China Rejects Fresh US Tariff Plans as 'Political Maneuvering'

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya said on Wednesday that the Bharatiya Janata Party's future chief ministerial candidate will be decided by elected MLAs following assembly polls, rather than predetermined. Speaking about BJP's internal process, he noted that the party contests elections under its 'lotus flower' symbol and resolves leadership through deliberations, with whoever is chosen unanimously leading. Maurya stated: "Based on that meeting, whoever is decided unanimously then leads." He added that while Yogi Adityanath currently serves as chief minister, whether Yogi or another leader will hold the position in the future cannot be determined now—the MLAs elected at that time will decide it. The remarks were reported by digital journalist Rohitashwa Ranjan of The Times of India.
items.title: UP Deputy CM Maurya: BJP's Chief Ministerial Candidate Decided by MLAs After Polls

items.summary:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged drinking water, with results expected within one to two months. FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani said on Monday that the process had started across the country and would take at least a month or two. He clarified that packaged drinking water was not selected for any specific reason but was part of the regulator's broader surveillance programme, noting that last year it examined dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, sugary drinks and other products. Punhani also stressed the need for food businesses to follow ethical advertising practices when making product claims, saying the issue involves not only legal compliance but also ethics.

The exercise comes amid regulatory action against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International over a sample collected from its Goa facility. On November 23, FSSAI granted sanction to prosecute the company after a regulatory sample was initially found non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Following an appeal by the company, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further examination, which also declared it unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). FSSAI clarified that the action applied only to a single sample from one batch, numbered GO 270, collected from Bisleri's plant at Verna Electronic City in South Goa. The authority issued an order prohibiting the sale of that batch under Section 36(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act.

Bisleri International welcomed the clarification, maintaining that the sales prohibition applied only to the specific batch manufactured at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025. The company stated it produces more than 50,000 batches annually and that no stocks of the particular batch were currently available in the market. It also maintained that retesting found bromate levels below the permissible limit.
