items.summary: President Donald Trump posted a meme depicting Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang waving a red bra in place of the clenched fist Trump raised after surviving an assassination attempt, celebrating Huang's return to his corporate role following an extramarital affairs scandal. The image drew criticism from commentators and observers who argued it degraded presidential decorum and reflected a political culture where powerful figures are held to lower standards than ordinary employees or executives; critics also questioned the message about fidelity given Trump's own history of marital infidelity, while others focused on what appeared to be a double standard in how personal conduct is judged based on an individual's wealth and influence. On CNN, guest host Elie Honig challenged conservative commentator Scott Jennings over the image, reminding him that Cory Comperatore died during the assassination attempt and asking whether his family was laughing at the joke. Trump separately framed Huang as a patriot and national asset while introducing an ethnic dimension by noting Huang was born in Taiwan and suggesting China might have recruited him to lead Huawei's AI operations if he had been treated poorly, conflating ethnicity with national allegiance according to critics. The controversy also surfaced disagreements within the Republican Party, as Senators Tom Cotton and Pete Ricketts questioned both Huang's reinstatement and the administration's intervention, insisting that unresolved national-security concerns about possible exposure of American semiconductor technology to China remain unaddressed. Trump has resisted following his party's hawkish positions on issues including China, Russia, immigration, tariffs, foreign policy, and federal government conduct, prompting questions about what constitutes a red line for him and the Republican Party; critics noted that no one could have combined these roles in a single episode by intervening in a private company's boardroom decision, vouching for an executive facing serious questions, and turning his sexual scandal into presidential entertainment.}
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang With Lingerie Meme Amid Scandal

items.summary: The slender loris—a small nocturnal primate known as kaadu papa (‘forest baby’) in Kannada and thevangu in Tamil—hides in forest canopy by day and hunts ants, termites, and small vertebrates at night. Its long limbs are poorly suited for leaping, so it depends on well-connected canopy and rarely reaches the ground; the species is mostly solitary and communicates through screeches, whistles, and clicks. Two global species exist: the grey slender loris (Loris lydekkerianus) in southern India and Sri Lanka, and the red slender loris (Loris tardigradus), found only in Sri Lanka. In India, two of four subspecies occur—the Malabar grey slender loris in Western Ghats wet evergreen forests and the brownish-grey Mysore grey slender loris across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh—with a few individuals isolated in urban Bengaluru parks and campuses.
items.title: Kadavur Slender Loris Sanctuary Established in Tamil Nadu

items.summary:
The recently opened Kurinji Garden at Chokramudi in Kerala's Idukki district attracted thousands of visitors who wanted to view the famous Neelakurinji flowers in bloom. While tourists visiting Chokramudi follow designated paths with numbers capped at 1,000 a day, visitors also access some other slopes nearby with the Neelakurinji blooms.

In August 2026, more than 4,000 people visited the Kurinji Garden at Chokramudi within five days of opening. Later reports put the total at nearly 8,000 within the first week. Visitors came from across Kerala and beyond to see the hills covered in blankets of a rare bluish-purple flower — Neelakurinji. Many said they came after seeing photographs and videos of the blooming flowers on social media.

"We came here after seeing the pictures on our phones… There is a bit of walking involved, but that's not an issue," said Ragini Anil, a native of Aluva, who visited Chokramudi in September.

At Chokramudi, the Forest Department has fixed visiting hours, marked paths for the visitors to follow and posted staff to manage the crowds. Plucking or damaging the plants is prohibited.

But the photographs on social media that drew people here do not say which slope they were taken on. Neelakurinji also blooms in other parts of the Munnar hills, including Korandakkad near Mattupetty, where access is not restricted to all.

So, people looking for the same blue slopes can end up in places with fewer controls.

Neelakurinji tourism in unrestricted areas On one such less-monitored slope in the same range, where the flowers also grew in dense clusters, there were plenty of visitors but there were no staff or official restrictions to manage the crowds. A narrow footpath wound through the blossoms, just wide enough for one person, and it looked as if constant foot traffic had worn it into the slope. Flowers grew within arm's reach on either side. Visitors climbed higher, where the flowers were denser and the views better.

Those walking along the slope often held tightly onto nearby plants to maintain their balance and avoid slipping.

Upon closer inspection, one could see that some flowers had already begun to turn brown, while others still looked fresh. Viewed from below, the slope appeared to be blanketed in blue; yet, a closer look revealed that the plants and flowers were at various stages of the blooming process.

Plants protected by law Neelakurinji is a semelparous plant; it flowers only once in its lifetime and dies after producing seeds. It follows a flowering cycle spanning approximately 12 years. While the majority of the plants bloom in the twelfth year, some may flower in the years immediately preceding or following that period. The growth of the next generation begins from the seeds produced after this single flowering phase. This plant is mainly found in the Western Ghats, including the Munnar-Idukki region. According to the 2024 IUCN assessment, Strobilanthes kunthiana is classified as a vulnerable species and in India Neelakurinji is a protected species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

The next generation of the plants depends on what happens before the seeds mature.

Amitha Bachan K.H., an ecologist with the Western Ghats Hornbill Foundation and an assessor of this species for the IUCN Red List, says, "The mass flowering reflects the conditions the plants have endured during their long growth period but does not guarantee the future stability of the population." Human interference before the seeds mature can disturb the soil and hinder seedling establishment, he adds. "The invasive black wattle (Acacia mearnsii), spreading from the nearby plantations, along with tourism and associated infrastructure development, also poses a threat to the species."

These concerns are also reflected in a report submitted by the Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanic Garden and Research Institute to the National Green Tribunal on April 8, 2026. The report says that Strobilanthes kunthiana has a limited and scattered distribution and identifies tourism-related activities, habitat degradation, and the spread of invasive plant species as threats to Neelakurinji. It also calls for long-term ecological monitoring of its populations and regeneration. Its recommendations include assessing the carrying capacity of flowering areas and establishing designated paths for tourists.

At Chokramudi, some of these approaches are already in place. The site has marked trails, staff to manage visitors, and a daily limit of 1,000 visitors.

However, that level of control does not extend to all flowering sites in the Munnar hills. In areas such as Mattupetty and Korandakkad there are slopes where the flowers bloom but they are located on private land; so special permission is required to enter them. In other parts of the Munnar hills, where tourist movements are not as closely monitored, there have already been instances of plants being trampled or uprooted. In September, the Forest Department registered a case against two young men after images of them allegedly plucking Neelakurinji flowers appeared on Instagram.

Bachan recommends designated pathways, soil-conservation measures, visitor-awareness material explaining the flowering cycle and pollination, and access restrictions in sensitive areas during fruiting and early germination. He also stressed the importance of protecting the grassland after flowering, when seed dispersal and seedling establishment take place.

Saju Varghese, the Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) of Munnar said in a phone interview that Chokramudi is an existing trekking and ecotourism destination, with visitors throughout the year. "The Neelakurinji flowering season brought an additional increase in visitors, as people also came specifically to see the bloom. Trekking activities continued independently of the flowering season."

While noting that there is no separate team for monitoring Neelakurinji, Varghese said "the entire Neelakurinji habitat is protected under the department's general forest protection measures, with restricted access and limited human disturbance." Access to visitors for viewing Neelkurinji was restricted to half the area to keep the habitat free from tourist disturbances for a more effective long-term habitat conservation, he said. Regeneration is expected to occur naturally under these conditions, Varghese said, adding that the next major flowering around Munnar is expected around 2030.
items.title: Neelakurinji tourism brings crowds, but not all areas are monitored the same

items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Himanshu Shekhar, a Delhi-based lawyer, for allegedly receiving more than ₹15 crore from Saurabh Chandrakar—the alleged mastermind of the Mahadev online betting app scam—in exchange for promising to influence judges, advocates, and government officials connected with the case. items.summary: In Vinod Kapri's 2024 film Pyre, the octogenarian couple Padam Singh Kapri and Hira Devi play Tulsi as they navigate a bleak landscape in Kumaon, Uttarakhand. The film opens with the pair invoking gods while traversing hilly terrain before Padam suggests that Tulsi jump off a cliff; the scene cuts to black and gives way to roughly an hour and a half of what one reviewer describes as circular spectatorship centered on waiting. A review published by Zainab S. Qazi, an independent writer based in New Delhi, compares Pyre to Samuel Beckett's Waiting for Godot, drawing parallels between the couple and the play's characters Estragon and Vladimir. The reviewer notes that both works explore existential loneliness, temporal loops, and companionship amid despair, with nature remaining indifferent rather than offering refuge as it does in Beckett's work. According to Qazi, the film's elusive figure—the equivalent of Godot who never arrives—is their son Hariya, whose presumed migration from the village becomes a microcosm of broader rural-urban out-migration driven by unemployment and poverty that leaves ageing parents behind. The review reports that near the end, it is revealed Hariya has long been dead while Padam continued writing letters in his name to sustain Tulsi's hope; Qazi characterizes this as an existential turn highlighting self-deception and constructed fictions. In what she calls the film's most haunting climax, a lone Tulsi mourns her deceased husband after he dies anticipating that no one would attend his funeral rites. The review also references related articles about how tourism, climate change, and unplanned urbanisation are transforming Uttarakhand.
items.title: Vinod Kapri's 'Pyre' Explores Loneliness Through an Octogenarian Couple Who Wait for Their Deceased Son

Congress leader and Lok Sabha MP from Saharanpur, Imran Masood, criticized the Samajwadi Party (SP) on Wednesday for announcing candidates for five constituencies ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections while seat-sharing talks with Congress were still underway. Speaking via PTI, Masood said 'We are not begging,' and insisted that any deal must be mutually acceptable and respectable. The remarks came a day after the first round of seat-sharing talks between the two parties ended without an agreement, as reported by The Indian Express.

The dispute centered on competing candidate lists: Congress had submitted 130 seats it wanted to contest in the Assembly elections, while SP offered just 26 seats across its 403-member Assembly. On Wednesday, SP announced Ashu Malik for Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan for Kairana, Umar Ali Khan for Behat, Mehboob Ali for Amroha, and Jyoti Lodhi for Lalitpur; the first four of these constituencies had previously been held by SP.

Masood said he would consult with his party on whether to continue seat-sharing talks with SP. He argued that holding negotiations while simultaneously making announcements demonstrated a lack of seriousness, questioning whether SP intended to contest Congress or BJP, and adding that it must be decided 'whether we want to fight the BJP or fight among ourselves.' Meanwhile, SP leader Shivpal Yadav said via PTI that 'everything will be sorted out' within the alliance.

Earlier on Tuesday, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav asked Congress to identify additional constituencies beyond the 26 seats already offered. On social media, he wrote: 'We will sit down together and assess which seats and which candidates for those seats are in a winning position,' adding that based on their assessment and 'the mathematical equation for victory,' they might also inform Congress of winnable seats it had not considered.

The two parties contested the 2022 state polls separately after their alliance failed to secure victories in 2017. In those elections, BJP won 255 seats with allies taking 18; SP won 111 seats with allies winning 14; Congress captured two seats and Mayawati's Bahujan Samaj Party one. On vote share, SP recorded 32%, Congress 2.3%, and BJP 41.2%.

The parties later revived their alliance for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, with SP allotting 17 of Uttar Pradesh's 80 Lok Sabha seats to Congress. In that election, Congress won six of those 17 constituencies while SP clinched 37 of the 62 seats it contested, bringing its total to 43.
items.title: Congress Leader Imran Masood Criticizes Samajwadi Party Over Preemptive Candidate Announcements Amid UP Seat-Sharing Talks

items.summary: Egg prices across India fell by roughly 10%-20% over the past eight-to-ten days after a bird flu outbreak in Tamil Nadu disrupted exports and pushed surplus supplies into the domestic market amid weakening seasonal demand, per The Times of India. In Namakkal, egg prices rose to ₹6.70 on November 11 but dropped to ₹5.60 following confirmation of bird flu in Cuddalore on November 13, a decline of nearly 19%. Prices fell more than 15% across most southern states while Delhi, West Bengal, Gujarat and Maharashtra saw smaller declines of 6%-10%, according to TOI.
items.title: Egg Prices Plunge Up to 20% in India as Tamil Nadu Bird Flu Outbreak Disrupts Exports
